extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors and newsroom staff seeking inclusive and accurate language guidance
extracted.subtask_description: A newsroom/stylebook glossary of terms with recommended usage, cautions, and examples to help journalists report about race, gender, disability, religion, nationality and other identity-related topics accurately and respectfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: coded language
rubrics_metrics.description: Substituting terms related to race or racial identity with seemingly race-neutral terms that disguise explicit and/or implicit bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include “inner-city” and “urban” as code for Black people, people of color or low-income people. Avoid language that functions as a code for race or class.

rubrics_metrics.name: codeswitching
rubrics_metrics.description: Shifting between two or more different languages, dialects, accents or modes of speaking or modifying one’s behavior or appearance to adapt to different situations or be accepted by different groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code switching is a learned skill requiring dedicated, well-trained teachers and exposure to linguistic varieties other than the home language. Use with explanation/ context if relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: codger
rubrics_metrics.description: An ageist term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid.

rubrics_metrics.name: colonialism
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical process beginning in the 16th century in which European powers subjugated peoples as colonies, with varied regional actors (Dutch, British, French, Belgian, Portuguese, Spanish).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains role in Asia, Middle East, Africa, and the Americas; notes post-WWII decolonization in 1940s–1960s. See related entries: Imperialism, Third World.

rubrics_metrics.name: colored
rubrics_metrics.description: An archaic term for Black; in some African countries denotes mixed racial ancestry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use unless referring to official names, historical events or in quotes. See African, African American, Black, black.

rubrics_metrics.name: colorism
rubrics_metrics.description: Occurs when someone with lighter skin is favored over someone with darker skin; exists within all races.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains historical example (brown paper bag test). Use explicit explanation when discussing intra-group bias based on skin tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: coming out
rubrics_metrics.description: Short for 'coming out of the closet.' Accepting and letting others know of one’s previously hidden sexual orientation or gender identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See related entries: closeted/in the closet, outing.

rubrics_metrics.name: commitment ceremony
rubrics_metrics.description: A formal, marriage-like ceremony in which two people declare their commitment to each other; may be of same or different sexes and religiously recognized but not legally binding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See civil union, domestic partner.

rubrics_metrics.name: community
rubrics_metrics.description: A caution: a synonym for neighborhood or town but a cliché because it implies shared like-mindedness a reporter cannot confirm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid blanket phrases like 'the Korean community' or 'white community leaders.' Instead, identify leaders and groups by name and, when possible, size or specific affiliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confucianism
rubrics_metrics.description: A philosophy developed by Confucius emphasizing social harmony and moral obligation; collected in the Analects; a philosophy, not a religion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use accurate classification (philosophy).

rubrics_metrics.name: congenital disability
rubrics_metrics.description: A disability present since birth (examples: Down syndrome, heart-related conditions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer phrasing like 'a person with a congenital disability' or 'was born with a disability.' Name the specific disability only when pertinent. Avoid 'defect' or 'birth defect.' See defect, birth.

rubrics_metrics.name: continuing care retirement community
rubrics_metrics.description: A community offering several levels of assistance (independent living, assisted living, skilled nursing) usually on one campus and often with long-term contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the full term when relevant and describe services/contractual aspects if pertinent.

rubrics_metrics.name: convict
rubrics_metrics.description: Term to refer to a person who is incarcerated or has been convicted of a crime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid this term; use people-first language (e.g., incarcerated people, people in prison, formerly incarcerated people) or a subject’s name and fixed biographical characteristics. Provides examples of preferred constructions and context-specific phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copts, Coptics, Coptic Christians
rubrics_metrics.description: Copt derives from Greek for Egyptian; refers to Coptic Christians who may consider themselves ethnically distinct from other Egyptians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use term accurately to denote religious/ethnic identity; be aware of linguistic origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: covering
rubrics_metrics.description: A strategy people use to downplay a stigmatized part of their identity to feel included in a group or sphere (e.g., work).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives examples (dyeing hair, changing eating utensils, avoiding bringing a same-sex spouse). Useful concept to explain concealment strategies; added April 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: crazy/crazed, psycho, nuts, lunatic, deranged, wacko
rubrics_metrics.description: Derogatory language that contributes to negative attitudes about mental illness and discourages treatment-seeking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If necessary in a quote, provide context to avoid reinforcing stereotypes; prefer 'people living with a mental illness.' Avoid using derogatory labels to describe people.

rubrics_metrics.name: creationism
rubrics_metrics.description: In U.S. context, belief that the Bible’s account of creation is literally true, often meaning a young-earth creationist reading of Genesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes alternative creation story in Genesis; see intelligent design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creole
rubrics_metrics.description: See Cajun, Creole (entry pointer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow related entries for correct usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: cross-dresser
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically refers to heterosexual men who occasionally wear clothes, makeup and accessories culturally associated with women as a form of gender expression, not entertainment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not synonymous with transgender; replaces the term transvestite.

rubrics_metrics.name: cruising
rubrics_metrics.description: Visiting places where opportunities exist to meet potential sex partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not exclusively a gay phenomenon. Use descriptively and avoid stereotyping.

rubrics_metrics.name: cultural appreciation
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeking to learn about another culture in a genuine and authentic way to broaden perspective and connect respectfully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differs from cultural appropriation in showing respect and reverence; added April 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: cultural misappropriation
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultural appropriation occurs when people use another group's cultural elements in ways that ridicule or are negative, common in media, costumes and language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some view appropriation as an assault on culture; contrast with cultural collaboration which can be respectful.

rubrics_metrics.name: DACA (Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Program providing temporary relief from deportation and work authorization for individuals who would be eligible for the DREAM Act; created by executive action in 2012 and renewable but can be terminated by later executive action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See DREAM Act; note program’s basis and precarious legal status.

rubrics_metrics.name: dead name, deadname
rubrics_metrics.description: Noun: the birth name of somebody who has changed their name (commonly used by trans people). Verb: to call somebody by their deadname.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be written as one word or two. Use respectfully; avoid deadnaming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deaf and dumb/deaf-mute
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical terms implying inability to speak or express oneself; often inaccurate and offensive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid these terms; people living with speech and hearing disabilities can express themselves in other ways; avoid conflating inability to speak with inability to hear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deaf-blind, deaf-blind
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicates a person has some loss of vision and hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the terms and capitalization the person prefers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deaf, deaf
rubrics_metrics.description: Lowercase 'deaf' for audiological status; capitalize 'Deaf' when referring to cultural identity and community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as an adjective, not a noun; prefer 'woman who is deaf' rather than 'a deaf.' Note some prefer lowercase or capital depending on affiliation. See related hearing-loss entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: defect, birth defect
rubrics_metrics.description: Words implying imperfection or inferiority when describing disabilities or congenital conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid 'defect' or 'defective.' State the nature of the disability or injury instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: dementia/senility
rubrics_metrics.description: Dementia is a general term for decline in mental ability severe enough to interfere with daily life; not a specific illness. Senility denotes conditions brought on by aging and is often misused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid calling someone 'demented' or 'senile.' Refer to a diagnosis only when confirmed by a licensed professional; use people-first language ('person with dementia') and, when possible, reference specific disease names.

rubrics_metrics.name: dependence (drug)
rubrics_metrics.description: A physiological state from regular drug use that leads to withdrawal symptoms when use is stopped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use accurate clinical language distinguishing dependence from addiction when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desi
rubrics_metrics.description: From Sanskrit meaning 'from the country' or 'of the country'; refers to people of Indian, Pakistani or Bangladeshi birth or descent who live abroad and implies shared values or bonds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pronunciation guidance provided. Use appropriately for people who self-identify with the term.

rubrics_metrics.name: detoxification, detox
rubrics_metrics.description: A process enabling the body to rid itself of a drug; medically assisted detox may be needed to manage withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that detox alone is not treatment but often the first step in a drug treatment program.

rubrics_metrics.name: developed countries, developed world
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms describing nations considered more economically and technologically advanced; CIA World Factbook list example provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally considered more current than 'First World.' Alternative classifications (WHO, IMF, World Bank) exist; see developed countries entry for nuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: developing countries, developing world
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms describing nations considered less economically and technologically advanced; CIA World Factbook list example provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally considered more current than 'Third World.' Note other classification schemes (IMF advanced/emerging, WHO income groups). See developed countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: dharma
rubrics_metrics.description: Pronounced 'DAHR-muh.' Mode of conduct conducive to spiritual advancement; in Hinduism refers to individual obligations, in Buddhism to the Buddha's teachings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use accurate religious/philosophical context when describing dharma.

rubrics_metrics.name: diagnosis, mental health
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless formally diagnosed by a psychiatrist or psychologist, avoid speculating about mental disorders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe specific mental illnesses only when diagnosis is confirmed by a licensed professional. Use precise terminology and avoid casual speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: dialect
rubrics_metrics.description: Language forms peculiar to a region or group, including pronunciation and syntax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using dialect if it renders the speaker ignorant or ridicules them; exceptions rare and require approval at department-head level or when dialect is news. If used, spell phonetically and be accurate; avoid exaggeration.

rubrics_metrics.name: diaspora
rubrics_metrics.description: A community of people living outside their shared country of origin who maintain active connections with it; includes emigrants and their descendants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commonly used for African, Jewish, Indian diasporas and often linked to historic events; use with historical/contextual explanation when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: different sex
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative to 'opposite sex' recognizing gender as a continuum; accommodates non-binary identities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'different sex' rather than 'opposite sex' when appropriate to be inclusive of non-binary people.

rubrics_metrics.name: disability discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: According to EEOC, occurs when an employer treats an applicant or employee less favorably due to a history or perceived physical or mental impairment; employers must provide reasonable accommodation unless undue hardship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting, cite legal definitions and note accommodation obligations and the 'undue hardship' standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: diverse hire, diversity hire
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms implying a person is hired strictly to meet a quota and suggesting lack of qualification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid these terms; instead focus on pipeline-building language like 'building diverse pipelines' or 'diverse slates.' Never describe an individual as 'diverse.' (Added April 2023.)

rubrics_metrics.name: diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Many kinds (race, gender, identity, orientation, class, age, origin, education, parental status, religion, abilities, geography, thought, experience); valuing diversity means recognizing differences as assets and striving for representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When discussing diversity, be specific about the kinds and avoid vague or tokenizing language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diwali
rubrics_metrics.description: Pronounced 'dee-VAH-lee.' Hindu festival of lights symbolizing victory of dharma and good over evil; observed also by Sikhs and Jains; word variant of Deepavali.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give pronunciation and basic context; note multiple religious traditions observe it and calendar differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: dog whistle
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of coded or suggestive terminology to subtly garner support from a particular group without broader audiences recognizing the message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term explains messaging strategy; added April 2023. Use to contextualize rhetoric that carries hidden appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: domestic partner
rubrics_metrics.description: Unmarried partners who live together, may be of same or different sexes, may register for some benefits; term used in legal/insurance contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See civil union; use term when legally/contractually relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: dominant culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultural beliefs, values and traditions that are centered in a society and thought of as 'normal,' marginalizing other practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting, clarify which practices are dominant and recognize marginalized cultures.

rubrics_metrics.name: down low
rubrics_metrics.description: Men who secretly have sex with men and may be in relationships with women and not identify as gay or bisexual; term originated among Black men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only in quotations or broad references because individuals generally do not self-identify with the term. See MSM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Down syndrome
rubrics_metrics.description: A congenital condition caused by an extra full or partial copy of chromosome 21, characterized by physical and cognitive symptoms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Down syndrome' (not 'Down’s syndrome'). Use people-first language ('person with Down syndrome'). Avoid 'suffers from' or 'afflicted with.' Use specific condition names when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: drag
rubrics_metrics.description: Dressing or acting in a style typically associated with another gender, usually through costume and/or performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not synonymous with transgender or cross-dressing; use precise labels (drag performer, drag queen) as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: drag performer / drag queen
rubrics_metrics.description: Entertainers who dress and act in styles associated with another gender; drag queen typically for performers portraying women.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drag is determined by costume/performance rather than performer’s gender identity; some drag performers are transgender. Use accurate role labels; 'drag queen' entry points to drag performer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dragon Lady
rubrics_metrics.description: A cautionary stereotype: a 1930s cartoon character portrayed as sexy and evil in Chinese silk gowns, popularized in later movies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label is caution; see 'china doll' and note it's a racialized stereotype to avoid.

rubrics_metrics.name: dreadlocks, locks, locs
rubrics_metrics.description: See hair, African American or Black (entry pointer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow hair guidance for African American/Black contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: DREAM Act
rubrics_metrics.description: Development, Relief and Education for Alien Minors — legislative proposal to provide legal residency for certain undocumented youth meeting criteria (arrival as minor, diploma, two years military or college).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes supporters' and opponents' viewpoints; see DACA for executive action counterpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: dressed as
rubrics_metrics.description: Phrase that can assume a subject’s gender identity or sensationalize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using it as a judgment that assumes gender identity; see entries for transgender, drag, cross-dresser.

rubrics_metrics.name: driving while Black, DWB
rubrics_metrics.description: Phrase describing racial profiling of Black motorists by police.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If used in quotes or copy, define what it means for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: drug abuse, substance abuse
rubrics_metrics.description: NIDA: drug use becomes abuse when illegal use or inappropriate legal use is repeated and/or causes negative consequences; addiction involves inability to control use and changes in brain functioning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clinical definitions; distinguish abuse, dependence, addiction; avoid stigmatizing language and be specific about behaviors and diagnoses.

rubrics_metrics.name: dwarf, little person, midget, short stature
rubrics_metrics.description: Dwarfism is medical/genetic resulting in stature below about 4'10"; 'midget' is now widely considered derogatory; 'little person' and 'short stature' have gained use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to short stature only if relevant; ask people which term they prefer. Avoid 'dwarf' unless in quote or medical diagnosis; avoid 'vertically challenged' and 'midget.' Follow Little People of America recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: dyke
rubrics_metrics.description: Originally a pejorative for a lesbian; being reclaimed by some.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offensive when used as an epithet; use only if there is a compelling reason. See lesbian.

rubrics_metrics.name: dyslexia, dyslexic
rubrics_metrics.description: A learning disability with problems identifying speech sounds and linking them to letters/words; chief symptoms: spelling, reading, pronunciation, auditory processing difficulties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to someone as having dyslexia only when relevant and formally diagnosed. Use people-first language ('has dyslexia') rather than using 'dyslexic' as a noun.

rubrics_metrics.name: Easter
rubrics_metrics.description: Major Christian holy day marking Jesus' Resurrection; Western and Orthodox churches often celebrate on different dates due to calendar differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate names and explain calendar differences; note Orthodox Christians may call it 'Pascha.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Eastern Orthodox
rubrics_metrics.description: Group of Christian churches not recognizing papal authority; split from Western church in 1054; includes Greek, Russian, Armenian Orthodox and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes governance structure, titles, and style guidance for references to clergy (capitalize titles before a name; use Rev. then last name on second reference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ebonics
rubrics_metrics.description: Slang or nonstandard English used by some in the Black community; also called Black English, African American English, African American Vernacular English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National Association of Black Journalists advises avoiding the term in news copy. References provided for further reading (e.g., John R. Rickford).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eid al-Adha
rubrics_metrics.description: Pronounced 'EED-uhl-ad-ha.' Feast of Sacrifice concluding the hajj pilgrimage observance; observed with prayers and a feast; date shifts with lunar calendar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide pronunciation and explain significance and date variability; see hajj.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eid al-Fitr
rubrics_metrics.description: Pronounced 'EED-uhl-FIT-uhr.' Islamic holiday marking the end of Ramadan, observed with prayers, charity and meals; date shifts with lunar calendar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide pronunciation and explain practices and date variability; fasting is forbidden on this day; see Ramadan.

rubrics_metrics.name: elderly
rubrics_metrics.description: Term appropriate only in generic phrases (concern for the elderly) and not for specific individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use carefully and sparingly; if describing individual faculties deteriorating, follow AP guidance to cite examples and attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emancipation Proclamation
rubrics_metrics.description: 1863 proclamation by Lincoln encouraging slaves in seceded Southern areas to become contrabands; applied only in seceded areas and did not end slavery; set stage for 13th Amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain historical scope and limitations; note relationship to Juneteenth and subsequent enforcement events.

rubrics_metrics.name: eñe, ñ
rubrics_metrics.description: In Spanish, ñ is a separate letter called eñe, pronounced 'enye'; substituting plain n can change words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve the tilde in Spanish words and explain pronunciation when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: English-only movement
rubrics_metrics.description: Effort to make English the official U.S. language; about half the states have adopted English-only laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note opponents argue such laws are divisive and racist; provide context on prevalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: epicanthic fold
rubrics_metrics.description: See eye shape (entry pointer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the recommended eye-shape guidance; avoid stereotyping.

rubrics_metrics.name: epilepsy/epileptic fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Chronic neurological disorder with recurrent unprovoked seizures; manifests differently across individuals; epilepsy is fourth most common neurological disorder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to someone as having epilepsy only when relevant and formally diagnosed by a licensed professional. Use 'seizure' rather than 'fit' or 'epileptic fit.' Avoid casual or sensational language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episcopal Church
rubrics_metrics.description: Part of the Anglican Communion; formally called Protestant Episcopal Church in the U.S.; governed by Executive Council and General Convention; has provinces, dioceses and parishes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Episcopal Church' in references; capitalization and title usage guidance provided for clergy (capitalize titles before a name; repeat title before name if no last name is used; Archbishop may be 'Most Rev.' on first reference).
